plugins.name: dsh-plugin-reactive-resume
plugins.verdict: The shipped plugin is 88 lines that do exactly one thing - hand your API key to the Reactive Resume origin you configured and mount its MCP tools - with no telemetry, no child processes, no dynamic code execution, and no credential path beyond the one environment variable the README names.

plugins.name: OpenViking memory plugin
plugins.verdict: Conversation data flows only to the endpoint you pin, loopback by default; no dynamic execution, no telemetry, no child processes from the plugin.
plugins.description: OpenViking memory and context bundle for DeepSeek Harness: pre-step auto-recall and profile injection, session capture, `viking://` URI guarding, and recall/write memory tools backed by an OpenViking server.

plugins.name: PicGo (`@picgo/dsh-plugin`)
plugins.verdict: Every network call the plugin itself makes goes to `127.0.0.1:36677` - the PicGo desktop app on your own machine - and the only credential it touches is that app's own auth secret; the far larger capability, uploading your files to a configured image host, is delegated to the `picgo` library and is precisely the advertised product.

plugins.name: WeKnora tools (`@wxg-prc-cpg/dsh-weknora`)
plugins.verdict: The plugin is a thin, well-typed HTTP client that registers up to four read-only retrieval tools against one WeKnora deployment you configure, with no dynamic code execution, no child processes, no filesystem access, and no credential path beyond the one API key that authenticates that deployment.
plugins.description: Four read-only tools over a WeKnora knowledge base: list knowledge bases, hybrid passage search, reassemble one document's chunks in order, and WeKnora's own cited RAG or ReAct-agent answer with a resumable session id.

plugins.name: awesome-gpt-image-2 (`gpt-image-2-style-library`)
plugins.verdict: The graded skill is inert markdown and JSON with a cpSync-only installer; all scanner volume belongs to the hosted web app around it, which never runs on an agent user's machine.

plugins.name: Archify (`@tt-a1i/archify-dsh`)
plugins.verdict: Host adapter is 21 lines of path math; all capability lives in the user-invoked skill CLI behind layered SSRF guards; no telemetry, no credential access.
plugins.description: Generate validated, self-contained interactive architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle diagrams from repositories or system descriptions.

plugins.name: modlens (`@liustack/modlens`)
plugins.verdict: Network targets only named vision endpoints plus its own loopback routes; credentials are touched solely for existence checks and opt-in reuse grants.
plugins.description: Vision bridge for text-only models: paste an image, get structured JSON evidence (OCR, layout, semantics).

plugins.name: dsh-better-sidebar
plugins.verdict: No telemetry, third-party egress, or credential reads; hands the model a real shell through terminal tools, which is the documented product.
plugins.description: Full sidebar workbench with file rendering and editing, terminal, Git, and subagents; third-party plugins can register new tabs.

plugins.name: NanmiCoder dsh-agent-teams (`dsh-agent-teams`)
plugins.verdict: The cleanest plugin this audit line has reviewed: zero network egress in shipped code, zero telemetry, zero dynamic code execution, filesystem writes confined to `<workspace>/.agent-teams/`, no npm lifecycle hooks; residual risk comes from what the product is - members are full-capability subagents and the npm install channel floats rather than pins.
plugins.description: AgentTeams multi-agent teams.

plugins.name: dsh-context
plugins.verdict: One cached npm version check, zero credential reads, no dynamic execution; system prompts and messages render in the web UI by design.
plugins.description: DSH context insight panel: Context dashboard + /context command + Context browser — one-stop context lifecycle management with categorized composition, content details, evolution trends, compaction/injection events, and stats.

plugins.name: dsh-full-remote
plugins.verdict: Exposes your DSH instance to other devices and does that one job defensively: 192-bit token gate with per-device sessions, hash-only cookie secrets, constant-time comparison, loopback-only control plane, CIDR allowlists, SHA256-pinned cloudflared downloads, no telemetry or credential access in shipped source.
plugins.description: Remote DeepSeek Harness with full server-side API access (`settings.*` / `credentials.*` / `host.listDirectory`). Token-gated reverse proxy, per-device sessions, phone invite QR, fence self-check, optional approval / CIDR / idle timeout / local TLS, WebSocket/SSE.

plugins.name: dsh-vision (`@linenxi-ctrl/dsh-vision`)
plugins.verdict: Sends your images and its one API key to exactly one place - the API base you type into its own panel - and nowhere else, but its one-click installer rewrites DSH configuration files and can download a Node.js runtime from third-party mirrors without checksum verification.
plugins.description: External vision plugin for DeepSeek Harness: whale-button config panel, image recognition with auto-reply, and agent screenshot/recognize tools.

plugins.name: dsh-read-url
plugins.verdict: A fetch-and-extract tool that talks to whatever URL it is handed and nothing else: no credentials exist to steal, no telemetry, no dynamic code execution in shipped files, and its one child process is curl invoked through your own configured proxy.
plugins.description: Read any page as clean main content: charset auto-detect (GBK/GB2312/UTF-8/Big5), noise stripping, compact text/Markdown, offset continuation, optional SPA rendering, batch reads and site crawling.

plugins.name: ponytail (`@mengyuly/dsh-ponytail`)
plugins.verdict: Shipped bundle has no egress, credential access, dynamic execution, or install hooks; the published npm tarball is byte-identical to the audited commit.
plugins.description: Port of ponytail: an always-on lazy-senior-developer coding persona with intensity levels, persistence of the default level, and review, audit, debt, gain and help skills for DeepSeek Harness.

plugins.name: OpenDesign design plugin
plugins.verdict: The DSH profile adapter is stdio-only with no egress or credential reads; install-time builds, opt-out analytics, and an auto-updating desktop app cap it at C.

plugins.name: Cherry Studio (`@cherrystudio/dsh-bridge`)
plugins.verdict: Bridge control plane is token-gated loopback with a fail-closed policy engine, but an unauditable obfuscated SSO vendor bundle ships in the main process alongside opt-out telemetry.

plugins.name: Reasonix
plugins.verdict: Nothing hostile was found and the security-relevant code that was read is unusually careful, but this is a full coding agent rather than a plugin: it phones home by default under a first-run consent prompt, its extension system grants sidecars the unfiltered process environment by explicit design, and what npm installs is a prebuilt binary this audit could not verify against the source it read.

plugins.name: distilly (`@titanwings/distilly`)
plugins.verdict: The installer is careful and small, but the payload it installs is a 7584-line Python toolbox whose whole purpose is to harvest another person's messages and documents out of Feishu, DingTalk, Slack and X, including by driving your logged-in Chrome profile - capable, honest about it in the README, and squarely a privacy instrument rather than a code hazard.

plugins.name: NocoBase AI plugin (`@nocobase/plugin-ai`)
plugins.verdict: Egress is admin-configured provider endpoints only, local file reads are structurally refused, no telemetry found - but real dynamic-execution machinery ships as product features behind an AGPL-plus-closed-pro-tier license, and the repo's dsh-plugin topic is unbacked by any manifest.

plugins.name: DSH Desktop (`dsh-plugin-desktop`)
plugins.verdict: Nothing hostile found: named endpoints behind a DNS-pinned private-range-blocking HTTP client and consent-gated updates, but installer validation is magic-only and market installs float to npm latest at click time.

plugins.name: voyager (Gemini Voyager)
plugins.verdict: A large, disciplined, GPL-3.0 browser extension with no telemetry and a genuinely careful permission model, whose grade is set not by anything it does wrong but by what it is: code that runs inside your Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT sessions, that can request `<all_urls>`, and that ships through stores whose artifacts this audit did not verify against the source.

plugins.name: learn-harness-engineering
plugins.verdict: Almost all 638 scanned files are course prose, translations, and student project scaffolds that never run on your machine; the executable surface is a read-only shell auditor and a small scaffolding skill with no network access, and the one real objection is that the README's headline install is an unpinned `curl \| bash`.

plugins.name: EverOS memory layer (DSH integration withdrawn)
plugins.verdict: Core is clean local-first Python with user-configured endpoints and zero dynamic execution, but its shipped Claude Code plugin sends every raw prompt to api.evermind.ai via session hooks, and the DSH plugin was moved out of this repo one day before audit.

plugins.name: MemOS memory plugin (`@memtensor/memos-local-plugin`)
plugins.verdict: The DSH adapter has zero egress by construction, loopback-asserted viewer, local-only storage and read-only tools; sibling surfaces (opt-out telemetry sender, admin restart/spawn route) and unverified npm provenance cap it at C.

plugins.name: Yao Agents platform
plugins.verdict: Nothing hostile survives adjudication of its DSH runner and skill injection, but the platform's own `secret_read` tool hands decrypted stored secrets to agent-invoked processes by design, the DSH path receives your connector API key through the process environment, and the license carries commercial-use conditions beyond Apache-2.0.

plugins.name: dsh-web family (`@linxin666/*` aggregation)
plugins.verdict: Nothing hostile found on audited surfaces: loopback-fenced routes, 0600 SSH secret storage, transparently documented telemetry - but fourteen plugins beacon dsh-market.com daily with no opt-out switch, an optional quick tunnel can publish your web UI publicly, workshop installs float to newest, and one bundled skin silently fetches stock-quote hosts.

plugins.name: OpenPencil
plugins.verdict: A well-documented Rust design app whose account sign-in runs through a closed-source prebuilt static library committed into the repo, while everything auditable (ticket verifier, relay endpoint parsing, MCP tools, user-configured AI dispatch) checked out clean.

plugins.name: ouroboros
plugins.verdict: No malicious indicators, but phones home by default (documented, opt-out), reaches pypi.org before consent, and runs floating PyPI builds rather than the audited commit.
plugins.description: Config-only bundle that mounts Ouroboros through the DSH MCP client, exposing 36 interview, Seed, execution, evaluation, and evolution workflow tools in DSH.

plugins.name: iPolloWork DSH Studio plugins (`deepseek-idesign`)
plugins.verdict: Design/PPT bundles have zero egress with token-gated, traversal-proof workspace routes and a provenance-attested publish flow; capped at C by unverifiable tarball-to-commit equality and a source-available parent license.

plugins.name: dsh-web-ui family (`@linxin666/*`)
plugins.verdict: No malicious behavior found on any audited surface; capped at C because the behavioral probe and cross-model review did not run, telemetry lacks opt-in, and SSH secrets sit in plaintext.
plugins.description: Git branch selector and Git graph for the dsh web GUI: switch branches and explore branch-lane and commit history from the conversation header.

plugins.name: PetDex bridge (`@petdex/dsh-plugin`)
plugins.verdict: The DSH adapter itself is exemplary - loopback-only token-gated delivery of a content-free session projection with hash-enforced tarball provenance - but installing it means adopting a desktop companion whose hook layer reads every tool event across all your agents, ships opt-out telemetry, and auto-updates from its own endpoint.

plugins.name: dsh-anchored-standard (preset collection)
plugins.verdict: A small, dependency-free preset repository with no network egress anywhere in shipped code and argv-form spawns throughout, capped at C by the incomplete pipeline and by what the product is: presets that deliberately reshape the model's first-request tool schema and inject instruction text into sessions, shipped by a project now in maintenance-only mode.
plugins.description: Two-phase agent preset for DeepSeek V4 Pro: the first request sees only bash+read (Minimal-aligned bootstrap), then the full Standard tool catalog after the first tool call or reply; ships as an installer bundle plus a manual preset directory.

plugins.name: mirage (`@struktoai/mirage-dsh`)
plugins.verdict: Nothing malicious found, but it executes agent-supplied code by design, its configured doors reach the real host, and the audited commit matches no published npm artifact.
plugins.description: Swaps the filesystem and bash providers for a mirage virtual workspace: file tools and shell commands run over mounted resources (RAM, S3, Redis, Slack, Gmail, Notion, Postgres) instead of the host disk, with per-mount read/write/exec modes, per-command sandbox routing (monty, pyodide, quickjs in process; docker, e2b, daytona remote), and installed CLIs (git, gh, slack, linear, ntn, gws, or one you register) as head words in the virtual terminal.

plugins.name: ReMe memory layer (`@agentscope-ai/reme`)
plugins.verdict: Zero critical or credential findings and an unusually clean egress map - every network path goes to a loopback service you run or endpoints you configure - but auto-memory ships your session content to that local service by design, its inner agent can call paid LLM APIs, and the incomplete pipeline caps the grade regardless.

plugins.name: J-Space Cognition Suite V3.7 (`j-space` skill)
plugins.verdict: The executable surface is two stdlib-only Python scripts with zero egress, credential access, or dynamic execution writing only a `.jspace/` ledger - the real product is ~1700 lines of assertive prompt material steering model self-narrative, capped at C by unverified benchmark claims and the pipeline ceiling.

plugins.name: VibeSkills / Vibe Code Orchestrator v4.0.0
plugins.verdict: Core runtime and installer are disciplined (offline default, SHA-receipted installs, overwrite-forbidden managed blocks), but installing silently writes bootstrap directives into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and equivalent host files with zero user-facing disclosure, one governed-mode path globally npm-installs an unpinned package, and 253 bundled third-party skills carry their own per-skill review burden.

plugins.name: dashi-taskboard (`codex-taskboard`)
plugins.verdict: Shipped runtime contacts nothing beyond loopback plus endpoints you deploy yourself and both scanner criticals are test fixtures, but LAN sharing is unauthenticated on a wildcard bind by default, the launcher drives the Codex desktop app over CDP by design, and the bundled skill steers agents into autonomous board-driven work cycles.

plugins.name: dshdesktop (`dsh-desktop`)
plugins.verdict: A disciplined telemetry-free Electron host whose renderer sandboxing and consent-gated updates check out clean, but it polls a vendor update feed every six hours, its market button installs `dshmarket@latest` at click time, and its optional phone tunnel executes a downloaded cloudflared binary whose pinned checksum is never verified.

plugins.name: dsh-tui (`@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`)
plugins.verdict: Source review is clean (no keylogging beyond prompt input, egress limited to a balance API and npm checks); the compiled artifact npm actually ships could not be verified against it.
plugins.description: Claude Code-style full-screen terminal UI: pixel-whale header, live status line, and streaming thought expansion.

plugins.name: BitFun DSH bridge (`@bitfun/dsh-acp`)
plugins.verdict: The bridge itself has no egress, no credential reads, and approval-gated sandboxed composition, but installing it means running a whole desktop platform with auto-update on and a first-party relay endpoint pre-seeded.

plugins.name: dsh-deep-whale skins (`@dsh-external/dsh-client-ui-skin-*`)
plugins.verdict: Cosmetic skin system with no telemetry and skins containing zero network code, but the manager rewrites `~/.dsh` profile patches and shells out to git, checks api.github.com for updates, and installs from a moving GitHub ref while shipping 4.6 MB of unreproduced build output.
plugins.description: Whale-girl skin series for the DSH Web UI (maid-atelier).

plugins.name: Token Monitor (`token-monitor`)
plugins.verdict: Every credential it touches (files, env vars, macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, `~/.codex/auth.json`) flows only to the provider that issued it and nothing phones home, but the breadth of secret stores read plus an auth.json write path gives a compromised upstream an outsized blast radius, and hub sync trusts whatever operator you point it at.

plugins.name: last30days-skill-cn (`last30days-cn`; agent skill, not a plugin)
plugins.verdict: Clean dependency-light Python with no telemetry, no dynamic execution, careful secret handling, and URLs resolving only to the eight platforms it advertises - but it drives a real Chromium browser, persists each platform's cookies to your home directory, and exists to scrape platforms whose terms it asks you to respect.

plugins.name: dshmarket (`dshmarket`)
plugins.verdict: Install path is well-guarded (curated allowlist, DNS-pinned SSRF defenses, zero telemetry), but installs resolve to latest at click time and backups can carry unmasked profile secrets.
plugins.description: Browse, search and install community plugins from inside DeepSeek Harness settings, with category filters, one-click updates, enable/disable, theme switching and configuration backup.

plugins.name: dsh-vision-router (`dsh-vision-router@2.0.1`)
plugins.verdict: Behaves as advertised and is unusually disciplined about consent boundaries, but its core function is shipping your images to a third-party endpoint: image turns go to OVHcloud's anonymous AI Endpoints without per-use consent, and it also spawns system binaries and can update itself through the hosting DSH CLI.
plugins.description: Free vision for text-only agents: built-in keyless vision chain plus pixel tools (Q&A, grounding, crop, pixel diff, colors, OCR, SVG trace, cutout, screenshots); paste an image to use it.

plugins.name: dsh-vision-toolkit (`@anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit`)
plugins.verdict: Nothing hostile found: hash-verified vendored runtime, mock-keychain blackhole-proxied headless Chrome, secrets redacted end to end - but the default vision endpoint is the author's own hosted service, npm provenance is unverifiable, and a mirror-first pip path with version-only pins caps it at C.
plugins.description: Vision for text-only models: paste an image and the model switches to a Vision Toolkit variant for image Q&A, multi-image comparison, long-screenshot OCR, screenshot-to-UI reproduction, element grounding, and pixel diff. No API key by default — images are processed by the author-hosted free service, 100 per machine per day; configurable to your own provider.

plugins.name: api-relay-audit
plugins.verdict: Touches exactly the key you hand it and sends it nowhere but the relay under test; capped at C because no sandboxed probe or cross-model review ran for this pass.
plugins.description: Runs local security audits of AI API relays and LLM proxies from DeepSeek Harness, producing Markdown reports for prompt injection, model substitution signals, tool-call rewriting, error leakage, stream integrity, and profile-gated Web3 risks.

plugins.name: dsh-browser (`@yuxianglin/dsh-bridge-browser`)
plugins.verdict: Content scripts on every page plus an agent driving your logged-in tab, yet all egress stays loopback except a user-clicked update check, password/card fields are masked before leaving the page, actions are origin-gated, and privileged bridge methods refuse non-loopback callers; defaults auto-share page reads and installs float on main.
plugins.description: Chrome sidebar extension that lets DSH operate your browser directly, no vision capabilities required.

plugins.name: dsh-at-file (`dsh-at-file` 0.6.8)
plugins.verdict: A single-purpose composer plugin whose shipped code performs no network I/O and no credential access anywhere and which never opens the files it references, capped at C by a dynamic-evaluation construct inherited from a bundled vendored schemastery copy and by npm provenance that could not be tied to this commit.
plugins.description: Codex-style `@file` mentions: search workspace files in the composer and attach their contents to prompts.

plugins.name: AI Novel Writer plugin (`@ethanyoq/dsh-ai-novel-writer`)
plugins.verdict: The DSH plugin itself is disciplined - no egress, no dynamic execution, every write approval-gated, browser clients barred from supplying paths - but adopting this repository means co-installing an Electron desktop suite whose model API keys sit in plaintext JSON, whose Windows builds ship an auto-updater, and whose release tooling pairs environment credentials with GitHub network calls.
plugins.description: Installs a dedicated AI novel-writing preset and workbench: revisioned local project assets, a compact side drawer, and native approval-gated single-file changes.

plugins.name: dsh-harmony-next (`dsh-harmony-next` 1.3.35)
plugins.verdict: The cleanest scan surface in this catalog line - zero criticals or highs, one low-severity string literal - with every byte of real capability living in user-invoked Python tooling that drives your local devices over hdc plus one documented Huawei download flow, capped at C solely by the incomplete pipeline and a release zip never verified against this commit.
plugins.description: HarmonyOS NEXT skill bundle for DeepSeek Harness with offline API references and DevEco, HDC, and emulator automation guidance.

plugins.name: modsearch (`@liustack/modsearch`)
plugins.verdict: Attested, clean code whose business is sending queries and URLs to search providers - exemplary SSRF fence, existence-check-only credential access, loopback-fenced settings route - but Firecrawl keyless mode discloses searches to the cloud by default and the pipeline ceiling applies.
plugins.description: Web search bridge for text-only agents: ask the web or X, get structured JSON evidence (search, fetch, citations).

plugins.name: dsh-web-mobile (`@dsh-external/dsh-mobile-nav`)
plugins.verdict: A client-side CSS/DOM shell plus a host-side response compressor with zero live egress beyond your own loopback DSH instance; every scanner alarm traced to a dev-only probe script or bundler mechanics, and the pipeline ceiling holds it at C.
plugins.description: Mobile-adaptive layout for the DSH Web UI: the sidebar becomes a content-hugging overlay drawer, the conversation gets the full width, and the settings panel becomes a near-full-width sheet.

plugins.name: dsh-web-search-pro
plugins.verdict: Does exactly what it says - talks to whatever search engines and platforms you point it at, including jina.ai readers, Exa's paid API, and login-walled Chinese platforms using cookies you hand it - with disciplined SSRF fencing, but broad outbound fetching on the model's behalf is inherent surface.
plugins.description: Persistent enhanced web search: multi-engine routing (DeepSeek/Exa/DDG/Bing/Jina + GitHub/Bilibili/YouTube/V2EX/Xiaohongshu/Twitter/Reddit/RSS), SQLite+LRU cache, userscript-style extraction, Playwright rendering.

plugins.name: deepseek-harness-remote (`ds-harness-remote`)
plugins.verdict: Noise IK end-to-end encryption with pinned peer identities, 0600 credential stores, and a loopback-only control plane, but by design it hands your session, workspace, and settings surface to any device on your account through a hosted relay you do not control.
plugins.description: Multi-device remote access for DeepSeek Harness: continue an active session from your phone, tablet, browser, or another computer over an end-to-end encrypted channel (Noise IK + adaptive relay/WebRTC transport), with device authorization, ApiProxy-only remote capabilities, and read-only file preview via dsh-file-viewer — no shell, remote desktop, or write access.

plugins.name: Tencent BrowserSkill DSH plugin
plugins.verdict: Near-maximum Chrome permissions kept loopback-only with consent gates, yet an agent can read logged-in pages on prompt-level rails alone, and the daemon auto-updates itself by default.
plugins.description: BrowserSkill bridge for controlling visible Chrome and Edge Agent Windows from DeepSeek Harness, with native browser tools, accessibility and VOM observations, screenshots, owned multi-session control, and a live Web UI overlay.

plugins.name: memsearch (`@zilliz/memsearch-dsh`)
plugins.verdict: All egress goes to well-known endpoints with no credential theft, but session hooks pipe astral.sh's installer straight into a shell unpinned, which hard-caps the grade.
plugins.description: Shared Markdown memory for DSH and other coding agents, with automatic capture, pre-step context injection, searchable recall, and memory-to-skill self-evolution through a review panel.

plugins.name: hindsight (`@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents`)
plugins.verdict: Clean on manual review of the DSH integration: egress goes only to the user-configured Hindsight server carrying the documented payload (prompts, transcripts, git history), no telemetry or credential-store reads, raw scanner F traces to test fixtures and bundled ajv; capped at C by the pipeline ceiling and an unpinned `uvx hindsight-embed@latest` download in daemon mode.
plugins.description: Hindsight, agent memory that learns: long-term project memory with auto recall and retain, knowledge pages, deep reflection, and per-repo memory banks.

plugins.name: ruflo / claude-flow
plugins.verdict: Nothing malicious found, but the CLI silently npm-installs patch updates at every startup and one workspace postinstall globally installs an unpinned tool.

plugins.name: dsh-routing-suite (`@dsh-external/dsh-super-injector` + router presets)
plugins.verdict: No third-party egress, telemetry, or obfuscation anywhere in shipped code, but a git install triggers an npm `prepare` hook that can fetch an unpinned compiler at install time, and the product's core is loading arbitrary local packages - including ones its ingest flow has an AI agent build from any folder you hand it - into the live harness via dynamic code execution.

plugins.name: desktop-cc-gui (ccgui; not a plugin)
plugins.verdict: The DSH integration is a disciplined loopback-first RPC client that refuses to spawn the host except on explicit request, but adopting this desktop platform means accepting an undisclosed Baidu Analytics beacon on every launch with no consent or toggle, an optional remote service that binds all interfaces by default, and bundled skills that execute Vercel CLI and Doubao TTS calls inside agent sessions.

plugins.name: codeg multi-agent workspace (desktop app; not a plugin)
plugins.verdict: Internals are unusually careful (OS-keyring tokens, minisign-verified updates, version-pinned adapter installs, fail-closed token auth over a wildcard-bound control plane) yet the grade is D: the headline install is an unpinned `curl \| bash` executing fresh release binaries into `/usr/local/bin`, agent provisioning runs npm lifecycle scripts at click time (force-enabled past ignore-scripts for one package), and adopting it means network-reachable control of every agent CLI on the machine.
